'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**At least one person is killed and two others are injured in an [[improvised explosive device]] bombing during a [[cricket]] match in [[Bajaur District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. '''Arts and culture'''
*[[82nd Venice International Film Festival]]
**The 2025 [[Venice Film Festival]] closes with [[Jim Jarmusch]]'s ''[[Father Mother Sister Brother]]'' winning the [[Golden Lion]]. [https://apnews.com/article/venice-film-festival-awards-2025-441dd2ad0b2346e5edebb3955e16c979 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Pakistan floods]]
**Five people are killed when a rescue boat capsizes in the [[Chenab River]] while evacuating people from flooding in the [[Jalalpur Pirwala]] area of [[Multan District]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], Pakistan, with search operations still ongoing. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1940210/five-drown-as-rescue-1122-boat-capsizes-in-multan-amid-flood-evacuation-officials (''Dawn'')]
*Six people are killed after a cable wire of a ropeway meant for material transport at the [[Kalika Mata Temple, Pavagadh|Kalika Mata Temple]] snaps, causing the cable car to crash to the ground in [[Pavagadh]], [[India]]. [https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/ahmedabad/gujarat-ropeway-accident-cable-wire-snaps-10234298/?ref=archive_pg (''The Indian Express'')]
*At least three people are killed, nine are injured, including six seriously, and others are reported missing when an under-construction bridge collapses in [[Karbala Governorate]], [[Iraq]]. [https://www.alarabiya.net/arab-and-world/iraq/2025/09/06/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%82-%D9%85%D9%82%D8%AA%D9%84-3-%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A8%D8%A9-6-%D8%A7%D8%AE%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%87%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%AC%D8%B3%D8%B1-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D9%83%D8%B1%D8%A8%D9%84%D8%A7%D8%A1 (Al Arabiya)] [https://shafaq.com/en/society/Bridge-collapses-in-Iraq-s-Karbala-Injuries-reported (Shafaq News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Immigration policy of the second Trump administration]]
**[[Deportation in the second Trump administration]]
***[[South Sudan]] repatriates a [[Mexicans|Mexican]] national who had been deported from the [[United States]], after receiving assurances from [[Mexico]] that he would not face [[Human rights in Mexico|torture or unfair prosecution]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/south-sudan-returns-deportee-us-mexico-2025-09-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Gaza war protests in the United Kingdom]]
**Around 890 people are arrested at a demonstration against the ban on the group [[Palestine Action]] in [[London]], [[England]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8rvly00440o (BBC News)]
*A [[Chile]]an [[Judiciary of Chile|court]] releases [[Americans|American]] pilot [[influencer]] [[Ethan Guo]] from detention in [[Chilean Antarctic Territory|Antarctica]] after landing a plane without [[Flight permit|authorization]], while ordering him to pay US$30,000 in penalties and leave the country under a three-year entry ban. [https://apnews.com/article/chile-antarctica-ethan-guo-influencer-cancer-pilot-d863cb023bd8305e6f9a968726f90ea7 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2025 Formula One World Championship]]
**[[2025 Italian Grand Prix]]
***In [[auto racing]], [[Red Bull Racing|Red Bull]]'s [[Max Verstappen]] secures [[pole position]] for the [[Italian Grand Prix]] at the [[Monza Circuit]] with a lap of 1:18.792, setting the fastest [[Formula One]] lap in history, surpassing [[Lewis Hamilton]]'s record of 1:18.887 at [[2020 Italian Grand Prix|the same circuit in 2020]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/sep/06/max-verstappen-pips-lando-norris-for-italian-f1-grand-prix-pole (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2025 US Open (tennis)|2025 US Open]]
**In [[wheelchair tennis]], [[Tokito Oda]] defeats [[Gustavo Fernández (tennis)|Gustavo Fernández]] in the [[2025 US Open – Wheelchair men's singles|men's singles final]] to complete the [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Golden Slam|career Golden Slam]] in the event. [https://www.olympics.com/en/news/us-open-2025-oda-tokito-career-golden-slam-whelchair-singles (IOC)]
**In tennis, [[Aryna Sabalenka]] defeats [[Amanda Anisimova]] 6–3, 7–6<sup>(7–3)</sup> in the [[2025 US Open – Women's singles|women's singles final]] to win her second consecutive [[US Open]] title. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/tennis/open/2025/09/06/us-open-womens-final-results-highlights-sabalenka-anisimova/85992797007/ (''USA Today'')]
**[[Marcel Granollers]] and [[Horacio Zeballos]] defeat [[Neal Skupski]] and [[Joe Salisbury]] 3–6, 7–6<sup>(7–4)</sup>, 7–5 in the [[2025 US Open – Men's doubles|men's doubles final]] to win the US Open, becoming the first pair to win the [[French Open (tennis)|French Open]] and the US Open in the same season since 2009. [https://www.usopen.org/en_US/news/articles/2025-09-06/marcel_granollers_horacio_zeballos_claim_2025_us_open_mens_doubles_title.html (US Open)]
**[[Erin Routliffe]] and [[Gabriela Dabrowski]] defeat [[Taylor Townsend]] and [[Kateřina Siniaková]] 6–4, 6–4 in the [[2025 US Open – Women's doubles|women's doubles final]] to win their second US Open title together. [https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4357593/dabrowski-routliffe-win-second-us-open-doubles-title (WTA)]
